claim: Analyzing 21 large libre software projects' CVS commit logs, only 3 (14%) show a stable 'code god' pattern where the founding core-contributor group never gets replaced; the rest show either full generational turnover (~8 of 21) or a mixed founder-plus-newcomers composition pattern.
stance_target: open-source project-level core-contributor turnover is the norm, not the exception, across a substantial sample of large projects
scope_conditions: 21 large libre software projects (GIMP, Mozilla, Evolution, GNOME/KDE/Apache/Mono/FreeBSD components), analyzed via CVS logs, projects starting as early as Dec 1993 through ~2005
quoted_support: Projects that are still led by founding core groups have been the less frequent, with only 3 cases over 21 applications under consideration.

claim: The unit of analysis in this study is the project-level 'core group' (top 20% most active committers per time interval, aggregated), not individual contributor tenure -- it measures whether the SAME people remain dominant, not what fraction of any given cohort of individuals survives.
stance_target: methodological distinction between project-level core-group turnover studies and person-level cohort-survival studies
scope_conditions: methodology section, applies to all 21 projects studied
quoted_support: The most active 20% of all commiters (rounded by excess) for that interval is what we consider the "core group". Therefore, for each project we identify ten different core groups, one per interval.

claim: A prior Debian-specific study (cited as ref. 9) introduced a contributor half-life metric -- the time for a group of contributors to fall to half its initial population -- reporting a value of 7.5 years for the Debian project.
stance_target: the 7.5-year Debian contributor half-life is the field's standard reference figure for OSS volunteer survival, cited across multiple papers by the same author group
scope_conditions: Debian project, cited secondhand within this paper
quoted_support: The authors propose a half-life parameter, defined as the time required for a certain group of contributors to fall to half of its initial population, which is of 7.5 years for the Debian project.
